title: Rust owns everything touching the machine; frontend is view only
context: OpenKaava has a Rust backend and TypeScript frontend. The boundary between them must be clear and enforced.
decision: Rust owns everything that touches the machine: reading paths, shelling out, deciding what is on disk. The frontend is a view. It never reads a path, never shells out, never decides what is on disk; it renders a snapshot Rust produced and sends verbs back. Two files exist as chokepoints: `src/bindings.ts` (the only file calling Tauri's `invoke` or `listen`) and `src/shell/contract.ts` (the vocabulary shells build against).
consequences: If a wrapper is needed, it goes in the chokepoint. Reaching past the door is not allowed. ESLint enforces region isolation with nothing grandfathered, so this usually fails before a human sees it.
